answer: The most convincing sybil defense prices identity on scarce work history: trust accrues only through verified completed tasks, so each account represents months of real paid labor. An attacker mass-registering fakes must perform that costly work on every one, spending more in compute and task fees than any bounty or vote reward returns. Like water eroding a knoll by an ocean of legitimate agents, a fresh account starts worthless and must wander the same expensive gauntlet, so attack cost grows linearly with identities while payout stays fixed.
